statement: Telomeres are tandem-repeat DNA caps (TTAGGG in vertebrates) bound by the shelterin complex that protect linear chromosome ends, distinguishing a natural end from a double-strand break and preventing end-to-end fusion.
effect_size: Structural/functional; repeat sequence first read in Tetrahymena, shown portable when transplanted onto a yeast linear plasmid.
population: Tetrahymena rDNA ends; cross-kingdom transplant to yeast; conserved to humans

provenance.primary: Blackburn & Gall, J Mol Biol 1978; Szostak & Blackburn, Cell 1982

confidence_notes: Settled molecular biology. Szostak-Blackburn 1982 (10.1016/0092-8674(82)90109-x) proved the cap is a general, transplantable function, not a ciliate curiosity.

statement: Telomeres shorten with each somatic division because DNA polymerase cannot fully replicate the 3' end of a linear lagging-strand template (no upstream sequence to prime the terminal Okazaki fragment) — the 'end-replication problem', a direct consequence of the replication mechanism.
effect_size: Deduced from first principles; loss of a terminal DNA stretch per division.
population: Theoretical derivation (Watson, Olovnikov), since confirmed empirically

provenance.primary: Watson, Nat New Biol 1972; Olovnikov, J Theor Biol 1973 ('A theory of marginotomy')

confidence_notes: Not in dispute. This is the fundamental reason telomeres shorten; everything contested in the domain is downstream of this solid base. Watson 1972 DOI 10.1038/newbio239197a0.

statement: Telomerase is a reverse transcriptase (catalytic subunit TERT) that uses its own internal RNA template (TERC/TR) to synthesise telomeric repeats de novo, restoring telomere length; it is active in germline/stem cells and largely silenced in most human somatic tissues.
effect_size: Enzyme discovered as a 'terminal transferase' in Tetrahymena; RNA template component shown 1989.
population: Tetrahymena extracts; conserved enzyme present in humans

provenance.primary: Greider & Blackburn, Cell 1985 (discovery); Greider & Blackburn, Nature 1989 (RNA template)

confidence_notes: Settled. RNA-template paper DOI 10.1038/337331a0. Somatic silencing is a deliberate tumour-suppressor setting (see cancer-paradox claim).

statement: Normal human diploid cells divide a finite number of times (~40-60 doublings) and then enter stable replicative senescence (the 'Hayflick limit'); telomere attrition is the mitotic clock that counts divisions and trips this arrest, and forcing TERT expression keeps telomeres long and bypasses senescence in culture.
effect_size: Telomere length predicts remaining replicative capacity (Allsopp 1992); TERT introduction immortalises normal human cells without (in that study) malignant transformation (Bodnar 1998).
population: Human fibroblasts/diploid cell strains in culture

provenance.primary: Hayflick & Moorhead, Exp Cell Res 1961; Harley/Futcher/Greider, Nature 1990; Allsopp, PNAS 1992; Bodnar, Science 1998

confidence_notes: Causal in cell culture (Bodnar 1998, 10.1126/science.279.5349.349). Harley 1990 10.1038/345458a0; Allsopp 1992 10.1073/pnas.89.21.10114; Hastie 1990 (in vivo) 10.1038/346866a0. Replicative-arrest mechanism solid; does NOT establish telomere length as a useful in-vivo personal biomarker.

statement: Leukocyte telomere length is a noisy, poorly-reproducible, weakly-predictive personal biomarker: the common qPCR T/S assay disagrees between labs, individual/tissue variation overwhelms the average age decline, and population associations with mortality/disease are modest, heterogeneous, and frequently confounded.
effect_size: Cawthon 2003 linked shorter blood telomeres to higher mortality in 60+, but later larger cohorts are inconsistent after adjustment; inter-lab CVs large enough to reorder individuals.
population: Human cohorts (leukocyte telomere length); multi-lab reproducibility study

provenance.primary: Sanders & Newman, Epidemiol Rev 2013; Martin-Ruiz, Int J Epidemiol 2015; Cawthon, Lancet 2003; Demanelis, Science 2020

confidence_notes: PREDICTOR-NOT-LEVER core claim. Martin-Ruiz 2015 reproducibility 10.1093/ije/dyu191; Cawthon 2003 10.1016/s0140-6736(03)12384-7; Demanelis 2020 tissue-discordance 10.1126/science.aaz6876. Real-ish at population scale, near-useless at n-of-1.

statement: Telomerase reactivation is a near-universal cancer mechanism for replicative immortality (activity in ~85-90% of human cancers), and Mendelian-randomization shows genetically LONGER telomeres are associated with INCREASED risk of several cancers (with lower risk of some non-neoplastic disease) — so lengthening telomeres / activating telomerase is NOT obviously beneficial.
effect_size: Telomerase in immortal/cancer cells but not normal soma (Kim 1994); ~85-90% of cancers telomerase+ (Shay & Bacchetti 1997); MR: longer telomeres -> higher lung adenocarcinoma/melanoma/glioma risk (Haycock 2017).
population: Human cancer surveys; Mendelian-randomization across many cancers and non-neoplastic diseases

provenance.primary: Haycock et al. (Telomeres MR Collaboration), JAMA Oncol 2017; Kim, Science 1994; Shay & Bacchetti, Eur J Cancer 1997

confidence_notes: Strongest CAUSAL claim in the file (MR approximates a lifelong randomized dose, dodging reverse-causation/confounding), tier marked rct-proxy. Kim 1994 10.1126/science.7605428; Shay & Bacchetti 1997 10.1016/s0959-8049(97)00062-2. Evolution silenced somatic telomerase as a tumour suppressor.

statement: TA-65 (cycloastragenol, from Astragalus) is sold as a telomerase activator; its strongest evidence is a small industry-funded RCT (Salvador 2016) reporting an increase in median telomere length vs placebo, with NO disease, function, or mortality endpoint moved.
effect_size: Salvador 2016: low-dose TA-65 increased median telomere length vs placebo (surrogate only); Harley 2011 open-label reported fewer short telomeres (uncontrolled, conflicted).
population: Adults; Salvador 2016 n~moderate, 1 year, double-blind; Harley uncontrolled health-maintenance program

provenance.primary: Salvador et al., Rejuvenation Res 2016; Harley et al., Rejuvenation Res 2011

confidence_notes: SURROGATE-ONLY, small, industry-funded; NOT an outcome claim though sold as one. Even if real, lengthening direction's safety is unestablished (cancer paradox) and no trial is powered for cancer signal. Harley 2011 DOI 10.1089/rej.2010.1085.

statement: Stress, meditation, and comprehensive lifestyle change associate with telomere/telomerase measures (Epel 2004 stress->shorter telomeres; Jacobs/Epel 2011 retreat->higher telomerase; Ornish 2008/2013 lifestyle->higher telomerase & longer telomeres), but all are small, surrogate-endpoint, and observational/pilot — consistent with telomere biology being a downstream readout of overall health, not a demonstrated lever.
effect_size: Epel 2004 high-stress women ~a decade 'older' on telomere length (cross-sectional); Ornish 2013 5-yr follow-up ~10 intervention subjects, longer telomeres vs controls (descriptive pilot).
population: Small human samples: caregiving mothers; meditation-retreat participants; low-risk prostate-cancer men

provenance.primary: Epel et al., PNAS 2004; Jacobs et al., Psychoneuroendocrinology 2011; Ornish et al., Lancet Oncol 2008 & 2013

confidence_notes: Canonical surrogate-over-read. Direction unestablished; bundled interventions; no health outcome moved. Jacobs 2011 10.1016/j.psyneuen.2010.09.010; Ornish 2008 10.1016/s1470-2045(08)70234-1; Ornish 2013 10.1016/s1470-2045(13)70366-8. something-beats-nothing: do the behaviours on their own first-line evidence, telomere readout adds nothing actionable.

statement: Cellular senescence is a stable non-dividing, non-dying state with a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype (SASP) that drives tissue dysfunction/inflammaging; most in-vivo senescence is telomere-INDEPENDENT (oncogene activation, DNA damage, oxidative/metabolic/proteotoxic stress trip p16/Rb and p53/p21), and senescence is context-dependent (also anti-cancer and pro-wound-healing).
effect_size: SASP is the paracrine source of sterile inflammation; 'fix telomeres' != 'clear senescent cells'.

provenance.primary: Coppe et al., PLoS Biol 2008 (SASP); Hernandez-Segura, Trends Cell Biol 2018 (cross-ref B)

confidence_notes: Telomeres are ONE entrance to the senescent state; the room is larger. Senolytic grading lives in B-aging-mechanisms.md §2 (mouse-strong/human-pilot: Baker 2016 10.1038/nature16932 genetic; Justice 2019 D+Q pilot 10.1016/j.ebiom.2018.12.052). Senolytics do NOT carry the telomerase/cancer paradox (they remove cells rather than extend divisions).

statement: A consumer telomere-length test is near-useless as a personal scorecard: noisy assay (poor lab reproducibility), wrong tissue (leukocytes, tissue-discordant, infection-sensitive), weak population-level prediction, and no actionable output (the recommended response is generic healthy-living advice you already had, or a telomerase activator whose direction may be net-harmful) — often sold bundled with the activator it motivates.
effect_size: Cannot reliably track an individual over time or change a correct decision in either direction.

provenance.primary: Martin-Ruiz, Int J Epidemiol 2015; Sanders & Newman, Epidemiol Rev 2013; Demanelis, Science 2020

confidence_notes: Cleanest single example in the manual of a predictor mis-sold as a lever. Conflict-of-interest: tests bundled with activator supplements. Spend on VO2max/DEXA/ApoB/BP instead (reliable AND tied to a decision).
